video_caption: The video opens with a static presentation slide against a black background. The top section of the slide is a solid blue bar with a thin red line underneath, displaying the white text "The Solenoid". The main body of the slide is white and contains further text: "Prof. Stephen Sekula", followed by "Supplementary Material for", and then "PHY1308 (General Physics – Electricity and Magnetism)". This text indicates the title of the lecture or material, the presenter's name, and the course for which it is intended, which is "General Physics – Electricity and Magnetism". No people or other objects are visible, and there are no visual changes or transitions throughout this segment.

The video segment displays a static image of a long, copper-colored wire coiled tightly into a helical shape, similar to a spring or Slinky toy. Below the image, centered on a white background, black text reads: "A “solenoid” is a wire that has been wound many times into loops." The entire white area, containing both the image and text, is framed by a black background.

A copper-colored wire is prominently displayed, wound many times into a helical coil, resembling a spring, with two straight ends extending downwards. Below the coil, against a white background, text reads: "A “solenoid” is a wire that has been wound many times into loops." This text defines the object shown above it, indicating that the coiled wire is a solenoid. The entire image is framed by a black background.

The video segment displays a white background with a gray, thick, ring-shaped object positioned horizontally in the center. Black curved lines with arrows, representing magnetic field lines, loop around this object, emanating from one side, curving outwards, and re-entering the other side, resembling the field of a bar magnet. A straight red line with an arrow at its right end passes horizontally through the center of the gray object and extends beyond it, indicating an axis. In the upper right quadrant, a red rectangular box contains the text "B_axis = (μ₀ * i * R²) / (2 * (R² + x²)^(3/2)) î", which is a formula for the magnetic field (B_axis) on the axis of a current loop, where μ₀ is the permeability of free space, i is the current, R is the radius of the loop, x is the distance along the axis from the center of the loop, and î is the unit vector along the axis.

The video opens with a grey, textured background that resembles iron filings, illustrating magnetic field lines. In the center, a red horizontal line with a right-pointing arrow indicates direction. Above and below this line are two rows of dark circular cross-sections, representing current loops, with the grey texture swirling around them to show the magnetic field. A red semi-transparent box in the upper right displays the formula: "$$\\vec{B} = \\frac{\\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$$ " (English: "B-vector = (mu-naught * I * R-squared) / (2 * (R-squared + x-squared) to the power of 3/2)"), which is the magnetic field formula for a current loop. At 0:01, the red line and the formula box vanish. The image now solely displays the two rows of twelve dark circles each, representing multiple current loops, with a clear empty space between them. The grey textured field lines are very dense and straight in the central region between the two rows of loops, indicating a strong and uniform magnetic field running horizontally from left to right. Outside this central region, the field lines are more diffuse and curve around the individual loops, highlighting how the fields from multiple loops sum up to create a uniform field inside a solenoid-like structure. The texture of the iron filings continuously subtly shifts throughout the segment, simulating dynamic field visualization.

The video segment displays a static, grayscale image that visually represents magnetic field lines. The background is black, and in the center of the frame, there are two parallel horizontal rows, each containing seven small, dark, circular openings, totaling fourteen openings arranged in a rectangular shape. Surrounding these openings, numerous fine, wavy, hair-like lines, in shades of white and gray, depict the field lines. These lines appear to flow into the circular openings on one side, pass through the central rectangular area defined by the rows of openings, and then curve around the outside to re-enter the corresponding openings on the opposite side, illustrating a continuous magnetic field pattern.

The video displays a static black and white diagram of a seven-turn (N=7) solenoid against a black background. The solenoid consists of two rows of seven circles each, representing coils of wire. The top row shows circles with dots, indicating current flowing out of the page, while the bottom row shows circles with crosses, indicating current flowing into the page. Magnetic field lines, represented by curved and straight black arrows, emanate from one end of the solenoid, run uniformly parallel and straight through its center, and then curve back around to the other end. A label 'L' with a double-headed arrow indicates the length of the solenoid. Below the diagram, white text reads: "A seven-turn (N=7) solenoid. See how the magnetic field inside is becoming EXTREMELY uniform? In fact, the equation for a magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is just: B_inside solenoid = μ₀ N I / L (where) n = N/L (leads to) B_inside solenoid = μ₀ n I". This text explains the diagram and provides the formula for the magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid, defining the variables as the permeability of free space (μ₀), number of turns (N), current (I), and length (L), and introducing 'n' as the number of turns per unit length.

The video displays a static image on a black background, featuring a diagram of a seven-turn (N=7) solenoid. The diagram illustrates current flowing through the coils: circles with dots on the top row indicate current coming out of the page, while circles with crosses on the bottom row show current going into the page. Magnetic field lines are depicted, demonstrating that inside the solenoid, the field is uniform and points to the right, while outside, the lines curve around from one end to the other. The length of the solenoid is labeled "L." Below the diagram, text reads: "A seven-turn (N=7) solenoid. See how the magnetic field inside is becoming EXTREMELY uniform? In fact, the equation for a magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is just:" (B_inside solenoid = (μ_0 N I) / L) and "n = N / L" which simplifies to "B_inside solenoid = μ_0 n I."

A black screen displays a white diagram of a solenoid, featuring seven turns (labeled N=7) of wire with current flowing out on the top section (indicated by circles with dots) and current flowing in on the bottom section (indicated by circles with crosses). Magnetic field lines, shown as black arrows, are depicted as uniform and parallel inside the solenoid, running from left to right, and curving around the outside of the solenoid, entering from the right and exiting from the left. A double-headed arrow labeled "L" spans the length of the solenoid, indicating its length. Below the diagram, white text explains: "A seven-turn (N=7) solenoid. See how the magnetic field inside is becoming EXTREMELY uniform? In fact, the equation for a magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is just:". Underneath this, the mathematical formula for the magnetic field is presented: "B_inside solenoid = μ₀ N I / L" (B inside solenoid equals mu naught, capital N, capital I, divided by capital L), followed by a definition "n = N/L" (small n equals capital N divided by capital L), which then leads to a simplified equation: "B_inside solenoid = μ₀ n I" (B inside solenoid equals mu naught, small n, capital I). This segment illustrates the magnetic field of a solenoid and introduces the formula for its magnetic field using the concept of turn density.

The video segment displays a scientific diagram on a black background, which briefly transitions to a dark grey and then back to black. The diagram illustrates a seven-turn (N=7) solenoid, consisting of two parallel rows of seven circles each. The top row shows circles with dots, indicating current flowing out of the page, while the bottom row shows circles with crosses, indicating current flowing into the page. Magnetic field lines, represented by curved and straight lines with arrows, emanate from and return to the solenoid, with the field inside the solenoid appearing uniform and parallel. The length of the solenoid is labeled with 'L' above the coil. Below the diagram, there is text explaining the image: "A seven-turn (N=7) solenoid. See how the magnetic field inside is becoming EXTREMELY uniform? In fact, the equation for a magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is just: B_inside solenoid = (μ₀ N I) / L n = N/L B_inside solenoid = μ₀ n I". This text describes the uniformity of the magnetic field inside the solenoid and provides the formulas used to calculate it, where N is the number of turns, I is the current, L is the length, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, and n is the number of turns per unit length.
